clients.name: Hartono Wijaya Kusuma
clients.sourceOfWealth: Inherited - family coal mining and energy group
clients.objectives: Preserve family wealth outside Indonesia; diversify away from the family operating business; fund a planned property purchase in Singapore in 2027

notes.text: Annual review in Singapore. Client is more engaged than in prior years. Father has begun handing over the family group's treasury function to him. He was clear that the Julius Baer relationship is meant to be the part of the family's wealth that is not tied to the mine. Did not want to discuss reducing the legacy shareholding, said it would be read as a signal by his uncles. Interested in yield ideas.

Client called about the energy rally. Very positive on the outlook for coal and gas pricing. Asked what products give him more of that. Discussed the shipping and energy FCN, he subscribed the following day. He is also looking at a Bukit Timah property, expects to need around SGD 9m for the deposit in early 2027.

clients.name: Ravi Chandrasekaran
clients.sourceOfWealth: Entrepreneur - founder of enterprise software business
clients.objectives: Bridge liquidity until the secondary sale of founder shares expected Q4 2026; build a diversified portfolio post-event; establish a family trust

notes.text: Secondary sale process is progressing, bankers indicate Q4 2026 at a valuation meaningfully above the last round. Client wants to avoid selling any listed positions before then because he views the tech complex as the best place to be. Comfortable increasing the Lombard line if needed.

Difficult call. Client was agitated about the drop in his technology holdings last week and the effect on his collateral value. Drew a further USD 1.7m to fund a pre-IPO secondary. I flagged that this increases his utilisation at exactly the moment his collateral is most volatile. He acknowledged the point but proceeded. Needs monitoring.

clients.name: Margarethe Voss-Brenner
clients.sourceOfWealth: Inheritance - late spouse's industrial holding, received Feb 2026
clients.objectives: Understand and de-risk the inherited portfolio; secure a stable income; German inheritance tax planning

notes.text: First meeting following the transfer in. Mrs Voss-Brenner is still grieving and asked that we not make any changes for now. She said several times that she does not understand what is in the portfolio and that her husband handled all of it. She described herself as someone who has never taken a risk with money. Risk profiling completed as Conservative. The portfolio as transferred is not conservative.

Client asked whether she should be worried about the news from the Middle East. Sent a short note. She replied asking whether her portfolio would be affected and said she would prefer 'something safe and boring'. German inheritance tax instalment of around EUR 3.4m falls due before year end.

clients.name: Chalermchai Suphanburi
clients.sourceOfWealth: Entrepreneur - agribusiness and food processing
clients.objectives: Replace salary with portfolio income from Q2 2027; fund a family foundation; transfer the operating business to the next generation

notes.text: Client is firm on retiring in Q2 2027 and handing the business to his eldest daughter. He wants to know whether the portfolio can produce USD 1.45m a year without touching capital. Concerned about the drop in his bond valuations. I explained the relationship between yields and prices but he keeps returning to the fact that the numbers are red.
Client forwarded an article about interest rates and asked whether he should move everything to deposits. Have not yet replied. Needs a proper conversation, not an email.

clients.name: Aishah binti Rahman
clients.sourceOfWealth: Entrepreneur - palm oil plantations and commercial property
clients.objectives: Align the portfolio with a stated sustainability policy adopted in 2024; diversify away from plantation assets; fund children's education in Australia

notes.text: Reviewed the sustainability policy the family adopted in 2024. Client believes the portfolio is fully aligned. She was not aware of the energy fund holding. The Sunrise Palm position is a family holding from before the policy and she considers it separate, though it sits in the same mandate.

clients.name: Nguyen Thi Bao Tran
clients.sourceOfWealth: Entrepreneur - electronics contract manufacturing
clients.objectives: Meet USD-denominated private equity capital calls and US university fees for two children; grow capital at a moderate pace

notes.text: Client needs USD liquidity for capital calls and the first US tuition instalment. Submitted a redemption on the private credit fund. Warned her about the gate. She was surprised that a fund she thought of as conservative could restrict withdrawals. Most of her assets are Singapore dollar denominated and her obligations are in US dollars, which has become more expensive this year.

clients.name: Alistair Pemberton-Hale
clients.sourceOfWealth: Executive compensation - retired physical commodities trader
clients.objectives: Fund a charitable foundation from 2027; leave a defined legacy to three grandchildren; protect real purchasing power

notes.text: Client instructed an additional gold purchase. His view is that the monetary system is being repriced and that gold has further to run. I noted that the position was already above the mandate's commodity ceiling before the purchase. He acknowledged this and confirmed the instruction in writing. Suitability waiver on file.

Foundation launch planned for 2027 with an initial endowment of around USD 12m. He wants to fund it from appreciated assets rather than cash. Long-held UK tax questions remain unresolved; recommend involving the wealth planning team before any disposal.

clients.name: Chen Wei Ling
clients.sourceOfWealth: Entrepreneur - food and beverage franchise operator
clients.objectives: Fund two children's overseas university education from 2027 to 2033; partial business sale in 2028; steady capital growth

notes.text: Eldest starts at a UK university in September 2027, second child two years later. Combined fees and living costs estimated at SGD 420k a year for six years. Client wants certainty on this and is willing to accept lower returns on the portion that funds it. Also mentioned she is in early discussions about selling a minority stake in the franchise business in 2028.

clients.name: Andreas Lindqvist
clients.sourceOfWealth: Business sale - divested majority stake in an industrial group in 2024
clients.objectives: Deploy sale proceeds into a long-term allocation; retain a residual stake in the former business; retire in Europe

notes.text: Second attempt at a deployment plan. Client agreed the allocation in principle in October 2024 and again in June 2025 but has not executed. He says he is waiting for a better entry point. I showed him what the cash has cost him against the agreed benchmark since the sale. He was quiet, then said he would think about it. Also unwilling to sell the residual Nordvind stake for sentimental reasons.

clients.name: Priya Nair Menon
clients.sourceOfWealth: Inherited - family trust distribution received 2024
clients.objectives: Long-horizon growth consistent with a personal impact policy; first property purchase in 2028

notes.text: Client is thoughtful and well prepared. She reviews the sustainability screening herself and challenged two holdings, both of which passed. Wants to start a first property purchase fund for 2028. No concerns.

clients.name: Tan Boon Huat
clients.sourceOfWealth: Entrepreneur - property development
clients.objectives: Orderly transfer of assets to four children; maintain lifestyle income; minimise disruption to the family property portfolio

notes.text: Succession discussion, fourth attempt. Four children, two involved in the business and two not. No trust or holding structure in place. Client is 78 and in declining health. The bulk of the estate is illiquid Singapore property. If anything happens before a structure exists the family will have to sell assets into whatever market exists at the time. He asked for more time to think.

clients.name: Cheung Kwok Wing
clients.sourceOfWealth: Executive compensation - retired shipping group executive
clients.objectives: Draw USD 1.1m per year to fund living costs and medical care; preserve capital for two children

notes.text: Client increased his quarterly drawdown to cover medical costs. He asked why his income portfolio has lost money in a year when he was told bonds were the safe part. Explained duration. He said he does not want to sell anything at a loss and would rather wait for the bonds to come back. Note that he is 71 and the longest bond does not mature until 2045.

clients.name: Zhang Meiling
clients.sourceOfWealth: Entrepreneur - cross-border e-commerce platform
clients.objectives: Aggressive growth; maintain a credit line for opportunistic investment in her operating business; eventual family office structure

notes.text: Client sees the technology drawdown as a buying opportunity and wants more, not less. She was dismissive of the suggestion that her exposure to a single name is high once the note is counted. Her view is that she understands the sector better than the bank does, which is not an unreasonable position given her background. Credit line unchanged at USD 4.2m drawn.

clients.name: Lau Chi Ming
clients.sourceOfWealth: Entrepreneur - Hong Kong residential and commercial property development
clients.objectives: Generate yield to service development financing; retain exposure to the Hong Kong property recovery; fund a Mid-Levels redevelopment project

notes.text: Accumulator settlements are running against the client. Drew a further HKD 4m on the facility to meet obligations. Client remains convinced the Hong Kong property market turns this year. I pointed out that the perpetual, the shares, the accumulator and his own development business are all the same bet. He said that is why he is confident.

Redevelopment project needs an HKD 60m equity contribution by mid-2027. Client expects to fund it partly from the portfolio. Reviewed what is actually sellable. He was surprised how little of it is liquid.

clients.name: Kim Do-Yoon
clients.sourceOfWealth: Entrepreneur - media production and artist management
clients.objectives: High growth; thematic and event-driven ideas; comfortable with drawdowns

notes.text: Client asked for the most aggressive way to express a view that the Middle East situation gets worse before it gets better. Subscribed the energy and technology FCN same day. He understands the payoff structure well and asked good questions about the worst-of feature.

clients.name: Yamamoto Kenji
clients.sourceOfWealth: Executive compensation - pharmaceutical group board member
clients.objectives: Retire to Japan in 2030 with JPY-denominated income; reduce dependence on employer stock; support elderly parents

notes.text: Retirement to Japan planned for 2030. Client will need yen income at that point and is aware that most of his portfolio is not in yen. He has held the employer shares since 2013 and has an emotional attachment to them. Board position means dealing restrictions apply during closed periods; next open window is November 2026. Supports his parents at around JPY 18m a year.

clients.name: Fong Enterprises Family Office
clients.sourceOfWealth: Inherited - textiles and logistics group sold in 2009
clients.objectives: Perpetual capital preservation across generations; fund G3 education and venture allocations; meet outstanding private markets commitments

notes.text: Capital call of USD 3.2m met from the sleeve's cash. Flagged to the family office CFO that between the remaining commitments and the gated private credit position, the sleeve's liquidity is thin. He asked for a full liquidity map before the next investment committee in October.

Investment committee review. G2 wants to keep the core mandate conservative. G3 representatives pushed for more technology and venture exposure in the next generation account. Unresolved. Private credit manager has now gated three consecutive quarters.

clients.name: Elena Marchetti-Wong
clients.sourceOfWealth: Entrepreneur - luxury goods distribution across Greater China
clients.objectives: Hedge against currency debasement and geopolitical risk; diversify away from the luxury retail cycle; Italian succession planning

notes.text: Client is pleased with the gold position, which she describes as the only thing that has worked. She originally sized it as a 5% hedge. It is now materially larger and she has not sold any. Separately her distribution business is under pressure from weaker Greater China luxury demand, which is the same theme as her largest equity holding.

clients.name: Abdullah Al-Mansoori
clients.sourceOfWealth: Entrepreneur - Gulf logistics, port services and marine chartering
clients.objectives: Build wealth outside the Gulf region and outside the shipping sector; fund a family office in Asia; long-term capital growth

notes.text: Client subscribed the shipping and energy FCN. His view is that charter rates stay elevated while the Strait situation is unresolved. Noted that his operating business benefits from the same conditions. He said the point of the Asia portfolio was to be uncorrelated with the Gulf business. It currently is not.

Client is planning a Singapore family office entity for 2027, around USD 5m of seed capital. He asked for a view on what happens to his portfolio if the Strait reopens and normalises. We have not modelled this.

clients.name: Grace Adeyemi-Lim
clients.sourceOfWealth: Entrepreneur - private healthcare clinics group
clients.objectives: Long-horizon growth; establish a healthcare access foundation in West Africa by 2028; buy a Hong Kong property in 2027

notes.text: Clinics group is expanding into Malaysia. Client wants portfolio growth but is aware her wealth and her largest holdings are in the same sector. Hong Kong property purchase planned for 2027, around USD 3.6m. Foundation ambitions for 2028 are aspirational at this stage.
